Citizen information portals: find reliable preparedness guidance

A citizen information portal can help when information is spread across organisations. Check who operates it, which sources it uses and whether its limits are clear. Professional design alone does not make a website an official authority.

Updated: 7 November 2026 · RedScore editorial team

On this page

  • Understand the type of portal
  • Look for traceable information
  • Find official warnings
  • Review location and freshness
  • Consider data requirements
  • Know RedScore's scope

Understand the type of portal

A portal may provide local government services, local updates or preparedness guidance. Read the legal notice and service description. An independent preparedness website does not automatically perform the duties of a council or civil protection authority.

Look for traceable information

Check sources, dates and affected locations. A report about another region may be less relevant than a local instruction. Important recommendations should link to an identifiable original. Summaries can provide orientation without covering every detail of the source.

Find official warnings

Use channels identified by the responsible authorities. The BBK refers to warnung.bund.de and explains NINA and Cell Broadcast. Check the authorities responsible for your location as well. A general portal can link and explain information but missing reports must not imply an all-clear.

Review location and freshness

A saved town can help sort information. It does not prove that every local event is known. Check the last update time and any offline label. A saved map or list can remain useful even when opening hours, access or the emergency situation have changed.

Consider data requirements

Many general guides need no account. Personal stock lists need understandable storage and access controls. Check why a service requests location or household details. Do not publish private documents in public comments; use appropriate direct channels for sensitive enquiries.

Know RedScore's scope

RedScore is an independent preparedness and information service with checklists, a personal preparedness status, selected reports and source links. It is not an official citizen portal or emergency control centre. Use the guides to get started and follow original official sources for authoritative information.
